newsitem.title: UK: UK truckers slate new EU jobs directive.
newsitem.headline: UK truckers slate new EU jobs directive.

text.p: A European Commission proposal on working hours and rest times would drive the cost of transport higher, raising the price of goods in shops, the British Freight Transport Association (FTA) said on Wednesday.

"The White Paper (proposal) represents bad news for an industry which is already subject to complex and extensive health and safety based legislation," said Owen Thomas, FTA's Head of Road Freight Policy.

Its "assertion that own account transport operators are not even covered by the exclusion for road transport flies in the face of both practical and legal realities...FTA will continue to argue for a far wider interpretation of its scope," he added.

The Commission proposed on Tuesday that EU rules on rest times should also apply to workers not currently protected. This would mean that groups of workers such as "non-mobile" transport workers and fishermen would be guaranteed the same or equivalent working hours and annual holiday.

The existing EU rule, which was unsuccessfully challenged in court last year by Britain's former Conservative government, excludes about 5.6 million EU workers, some 3.5 million of them in the transport sector.
The FTA said the proposals recognise some need for flexibility in the industry, but its overall implications remain of great concern to vehicle operators.

In a survey of its members, the FTA found over 50 percent of lorry operators would have to increase the size of their to maintain current service levels as a result of the EU proposals. Nearly half anticipated the need for an increase of 10 percent or more in their fleets.
EU governments, management and labour groups will be asked to comment on the proposals by November.
